question.text: What road rights do bicycles have, and when may riders leave the lane edge?

answer.text: Bikes count as vehicles with full road rights off limited ways, may exit lanes for narrow roads, hazards, and lefts, may own narrow lanes, and yield to walkers on sidewalks.

teaching.text: A bicycle is a vehicle with full road rights except on limited-access ways, its rider may leave the edge for narrow roads, hazards and left turns, may take a narrow lane, and yields to walkers on sidewalks. Remember: Bikes are vehicles too.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Bikes count as vehicles with full road rights off limited ways, may exit lanes for narrow roads, hazards, and lefts, may own narrow lanes, and yield to walkers on sidewalks.

question.text: How much room must drivers give when passing a rider?

answer.text: Drivers clear bikes by three feet with slowed care, and pass two-lane riders like slow vehicles only when safe.

teaching.text: Give a rider at least three feet and slow down when passing, and on two-lane roads pass a rider the way you would a slow vehicle, only when safe. Remember: Three feet, slowly.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Drivers clear bikes by three feet with slowed care, and pass two-lane riders like slow vehicles only when safe.

question.text: How should drivers treat riders at crossings and when turning?

answer.text: Crossings treat riders as straight-through vehicles owed yields, and lane-crossing turns finish behind them.

teaching.text: At crossings, treat a rider as a vehicle going straight that you must yield to, and finish any turn across the rider's lane behind them. Remember: Turn behind the rider.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Crossings treat riders as straight-through vehicles owed yields, and lane-crossing turns finish behind them.

question.text: What safety rules apply to motorists around bicyclists regarding following, beams, doors, and horns?

answer.text: Motorists must not follow a bicyclist too closely, should avoid high-beam headlights at night when a bicyclist approaches, must check for bicyclists approaching from behind before opening a car door, and should avoid honking and startling a bicyclist.

teaching.text: Never tailgate a rider, shine high beams at them, open a door into them or startle them with the horn. Remember: Space, low beams, check doors.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Motorists must not follow a bicyclist too closely, should avoid high-beam headlights at night when a bicyclist approaches, must check for bicyclists approaching from behind before opening a car door, and should avoid honking and startling a bicyclist.

question.text: What rights and lane uses do bicycles have?

answer.text: Bikes own vehicle rights off limited ways, lane exits for safety, and narrow-lane ownership.

teaching.text: A bicycle has vehicle rights except on limited ways, may leave the edge for safety, and may take a narrow lane. Remember: Narrow lane? Rider owns it.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Bikes own vehicle rights off limited ways, lane exits for safety, and narrow-lane ownership.

question.text: How do drivers pass riders on two-lane roads?

answer.text: Passing clears three feet slowed, treating two-lane riders as slow vehicles.

teaching.text: Pass a rider with three feet and a slower speed, treating them on two-lane roads like a slow vehicle. Remember: Pass riders like slow vehicles.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Passing clears three feet slowed, treating two-lane riders as slow vehicles.

question.text: How do drivers read and yield to riders at crossings?

answer.text: Crossings read riders straight absent signals, yield fully, and turn behind them.

teaching.text: Assume a rider at a crossing is going straight, yield to them, and turn behind them. Remember: Riders go straight, yield.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Crossings read riders straight absent signals, yield fully, and turn behind them.

question.text: Which driver actions threaten riders?

answer.text: Tailgating, high beams, dooring, and horn blasts all threaten riders.

teaching.text: Tailgating, high beams, opening doors and horn blasts are all listed as threats to riders. Remember: High beams threaten riders.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Tailgating, high beams, dooring, and horn blasts all threaten riders.

question.text: Where do riders ride, and when may they take the full lane?

answer.text: Riders obey all controls, slow into lanes or right edges, own full lanes for lefts, passes, hazards, and narrows, may left-ride wide one-ways, and hand-signal turns.

teaching.text: Riders obey every traffic control, keep to a lane or the right edge when slow, take the full lane for left turns, passing, hazards and narrow lanes, may ride left on wide one-ways, and signal turns by hand. Remember: Full lane for lefts, hazards.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Riders obey all controls, slow into lanes or right edges, own full lanes for lefts, passes, hazards, and narrows, may left-ride wide one-ways, and hand-signal turns.

question.text: May riders hitch onto vehicles, and what rules apply on sidewalks?

answer.text: Riders never hitch vehicles, and sidewalk riders hold walker rights while yielding and signaling passes audibly.

teaching.text: Riders never hold onto moving vehicles, and on sidewalks they have walker rights but must yield and give an audible signal before passing. Remember: Never hitch a ride.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Riders never hitch vehicles, and sidewalk riders hold walker rights while yielding and signaling passes audibly.

question.text: What lights, brakes and helmets do riders need?

answer.text: Night riders shine white five hundred feet ahead and red six hundred behind, brake twenty-five feet from ten miles per hour, and helmet all under-sixteen riders.

teaching.text: At night a bike needs a white light seen five hundred feet ahead and a red light seen six hundred feet behind, brakes that stop within twenty-five feet from ten miles per hour, and helmets for all riders under sixteen. Remember: White front, red rear.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Night riders shine white five hundred feet ahead and red six hundred behind, brake twenty-five feet from ten miles per hour, and helmet all under-sixteen riders.

question.text: Which young riders need a child carrier?

answer.text: Under-four or forty-pound riders need child carriers, and carriers never sit unattended off rider control.

teaching.text: Children under four years old or forty pounds ride in a child carrier, and the carrier is never left alone out of the rider's control. Remember: Under four or forty pounds.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Under-four or forty-pound riders need child carriers, and carriers never sit unattended off rider control.

question.text: What rules cover group riding, earbuds and impairment?

answer.text: Groups cap two-abreast off bike paths and single up when blocking, roadways ban dual earbuds, and drink and drugs ban biking.

teaching.text: Groups ride no more than two abreast except on bike paths and single up when blocking traffic, dual earbuds are banned on roadways, and riding on alcohol or drugs is banned. Remember: Two abreast at most.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Groups cap two-abreast off bike paths and single up when blocking, roadways ban dual earbuds, and drink and drugs ban biking.

question.text: Which safety tips does the handbook give riders?

answer.text: Tips helmet every age, grip both bars, glance before shifting, flash neon and reflective gear, and pocket phones.

teaching.text: The handbook suggests a helmet at every age, both hands on the bars, a look before moving over, bright reflective gear, and a phone kept in your pocket. Remember: Helmet at every age.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Tips helmet every age, grip both bars, glance before shifting, flash neon and reflective gear, and pocket phones.

question.text: When do riders keep right, and when may they take the full lane?

answer.text: Slow riders hug lanes or right edges while lefts, passes, hazards, and narrows free full lanes.

teaching.text: Slow riders stay in a lane or at the right edge, while left turns, passing, hazards and narrow lanes let them take the full lane. Remember: Slow riders keep right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Slow riders hug lanes or right edges while lefts, passes, hazards, and narrows free full lanes.

question.text: What do the hitching and sidewalk rules say?

answer.text: Hitching bans outright while sidewalks grant walker rights with yields and audible passes.

teaching.text: Hitching onto vehicles is banned, and sidewalk riders keep walker rights while yielding and warning audibly before passing. Remember: Sidewalk riders yield to walkers.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Hitching bans outright while sidewalks grant walker rights with yields and audible passes.

question.text: What are the night light and brake distances for bicycles?

answer.text: Night kit pairs five hundred-foot white fronts with six hundred-foot red rears, brakes stop twenty-five feet from ten miles per hour, and under-sixteen heads helmet.

teaching.text: Bike lights reach five hundred feet ahead in white and six hundred feet behind in red, brakes stop in twenty-five feet from ten miles per hour, and under-sixteens wear helmets. Remember: Five hundred, six hundred, twenty-five.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Night kit pairs five hundred-foot white fronts with six hundred-foot red rears, brakes stop twenty-five feet from ten miles per hour, and under-sixteen heads helmet.

question.text: What do the carrier, pairs, earbud and sobriety rules require?

answer.text: Young light riders carrier up attended, pairs cap doubles off paths, ears stay half open, and sobriety rules.

teaching.text: Small, young children ride in an attended carrier, groups stay two abreast at most, one ear stays free, and riders stay sober. Remember: No riding impaired.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Young light riders carrier up attended, pairs cap doubles off paths, ears stay half open, and sobriety rules.

question.text: Where are a big rig's blind areas?

answer.text: Big rigs blind front, rear, and both flanks, hiding whole cars despite mirror banks.

teaching.text: A big rig cannot see in front, behind or along either side, and those blind areas can hide a whole car even with all its mirrors. Remember: Front, back and both sides.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Big rigs blind front, rear, and both flanks, hiding whole cars despite mirror banks.

question.text: What rules apply when following or stopping behind a commercial motor vehicle?

answer.text: Motorists must not tailgate a commercial motor vehicle, must leave space when stopped behind one on an upgrade in case it drifts back when starting while staying left in the lane to remain visible, and must not use high-beam headlights when following one at night.

teaching.text: Following a big rig, never tailgate, move to the left on uphill grades so you can be seen, and dim your lights at night. Remember: Give rigs room behind.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Motorists must not tailgate a commercial motor vehicle, must leave space when stopped behind one on an upgrade in case it drifts back when starting while staying left in the lane to remain visible, and must not use high-beam headlights when following one at night.

question.text: Where are the No Zones around big rigs?

answer.text: No Zones blind every side of big rigs despite mirror banks.

teaching.text: No Zones surround a big rig on every side, and its mirrors do not remove them. Remember: Mirrors cannot cover No Zones.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: No Zones blind every side of big rigs despite mirror banks.

question.text: What should you do when stopped behind a commercial vehicle on an upgrade or following at night?

answer.text: Avoid tailgating commercial motor vehicles, leave room and keep left in your lane for visibility when stopped behind one on an upgrade in case it drifts backward on startup, and keep high beams off when following one at night.

teaching.text: Stay well back from a rig, move left on upgrades to be seen, and dim your lights behind it at night. Remember: Dim beams behind rigs.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Avoid tailgating commercial motor vehicles, leave room and keep left in your lane for visibility when stopped behind one on an upgrade in case it drifts backward on startup, and keep high beams off when following one at night.

hooks_spoken: Bicycles are vehicles with road rights, so pass them with three feet and turn behind them at crossings.
